title: The role of recrystallization and grain growth in optimizing the sheet texture of magnesium alloys with calcium addition during annealing

nodes.label: Strong basal texture of rolled Mg sheet limits formability; weak, RD-split, tilted textures are wanted
Whether recrystallization or grain growth turns the double-peak texture single-peak, and how Ca weakens texture, is unclear
Basal sharpening comes from grain growth; Ca-bearing particles curb growth and diversify nuclei, preserving weak texture
AZ31 sheet as the reference Mg alloy
Add 0.5 wt% Ca to AZ31 (AZX310)
Annealing time 10 s-1 h at 250 C; 10 s isochronal 180-525 C; AZX310 growth kinetics 250-450 C
Two-step anneal: 180 C/5 h completes static recrystallization without growth, then 250 C isolates grain growth

nodes.label: Zener pinning by nano particles (plus possible Ca solute drag) stagnates growth; the effect weakens at 450 C and above
Zener drag pressure P_z = 3F_v*gamma_b/2r
Below 450 C AZX310 keeps a weak (~4 MRD), RD-split, tilted texture; at 450 C and above it turns single-peak
Ca-induced heterogeneous deformation broadens recrystallization nucleus orientations, weakening the annealing texture
GOS-split microtextures: softening from deformed to recrystallized larger in AZX310 (max 12->3.9) than AZ31 (8.3->5.3)

notes: Texture paper with no measured property: the spine ends in STR/MEC and design guidance; formability (the need) is never measured. Two branches: AZ31 decoupling (two-step anneal, b7->b10->b18/b19->b20) and Ca (b27->b32->b30->b34, b35). Figures opened: F7, F8, F11, F12; nodes on F2, F3, F4, F6, F10 carry image_checked=false.
